angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 534,298 km at 100.37 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 9.9636 +/- 0.0149 mas (same row, RUWE 0.87): 100.37 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.768 +/- 0.019 solar radii from Maciejewski et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-84 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.525L..43M/abstract): 534,298 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.853 +/- 0.038 solar masses from Maciejewski et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-84 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.525L..43M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5300 +/- 100 K from Bonomo et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of WASP-84 b's parameter set from Bonomo et al. 2017 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bonomo et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of WASP-84 b's parameter set from Bonomo et al. 2017 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-84.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.598, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-84 (pscomppars): spectral type K0, from Maciejewski et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.525L..43M/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, BD+02 2056: main object type Em*, Emission-line Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-84 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0 dex, from Kokori et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJS..265....4K/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-84 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.325, from Gaia DR2 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A&A...616A...1G/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-84 (pscomppars): age 2.1 Gyr, from Anderson et al. 2015 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...800L...9A/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-84 (pscomppars): rotation period 14.36 d, from Bonomo et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract)

rotationPeriodsCatalogued.source: VizieR J/A+A/705/A142/tablea1 (Physical properties study of planet systems), column Prot: 14.36 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place

projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-84 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 2.558 km/s, from Anderson et al. 2015 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...800L...9A/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.768 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.946. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
